claims.text: Special access contracts are 'carved out of the Defense Investigative Service's periodic inspection program', following a 1965 DoD decision that special access programs 'would be excluded from supervision by the Defense Investigative Service'.

claims.locator: 24 July 1986, describing GAO/GGD-83-43 -- the earlier report was not read
claims.sourceText: GAO accession 130581, 24 July 1986, describing GAO/GGD-83-43 -- the earlier report was not read
claims.text: GAO/GGD-83-43 of 18 February 1983, 'Further Improvements Needed in Department of Defense Oversight of Special Access (Carve-Out) Contracts', recommended change and DoD refused. The 1986 testimony gives DoD's stated reasons, including that 'access by Service inspectors would proliferate access beyond the minimum number of persons necessary.' The 1983 report itself was not opened in this pass.

claims.sourceText: GAO accession 130581, statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986
claims.text: GAO explains the term: special access contracts are 'carved out of the Defense Investigative Service's periodic inspection program', and 'In 1983, we estimated that there probably were several thousand such contracts.'

claims.locator: statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986

claims.sourceText: GAO accession 130581, statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986
claims.text: Lockheed reported 1,460 discrepancies: 'The current inventory of all 53 document control substations has been completed, and Lockheed has reported 1,460 discrepancies.' The inventory 'consists of about 40,000 secret and top-secret items.'

claims.nodeLabel: GAO accession 130581 - Controls Over Classified Documents for a Special Access Program at Lockheed Corporation
claims.sourceText: GAO/NSIAD-86-191, 7 August 1986; and GAO accession 130581, footnote
claims.text: The companion report names 'the Lockheed/Burbank plant', which the testimony itself does not. The testimony carries a footnote explaining why: 'As part of DOD granting us access to the special access program to respond your request, we agreed not to identify the nature of the program or the specific DOD component or military service involved.'

claims.locator: statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986
claims.nodeLabel: GAO accession 130581 - Controls Over Classified Documents for a Special Access Program at Lockheed Corporation
claims.sourceText: GAO accession 130581, statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986
claims.text: GAO states the exclusion as a standing policy decision: 'In 1965, DOD decided that special access programs, because of their especially sensitive nature and small number, would be excluded from supervision by the Defense Investigative Service.'

claims.locator: statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986
claims.nodeLabel: GAO accession 130581 - Controls Over Classified Documents for a Special Access Program at Lockheed Corporation
claims.sourceText: GAO accession 130581, statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986
claims.text: The unaccounted-for total is 11, not 17 or 46: 'Lockheed's reported results --which we have not yet had the opportunity to verify-- are that 224 documents were later accounted for, and 11 were unresolved ... Lockheed says 7 of the 11 unresolved documents were inadvertently destroyed and it could not locate the other 4.' The 46 destroyed and the 17 transferred out of the company are dispositions within the 224 accounted for.

claims.locator: statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986
claims.nodeLabel: GAO accession 130581 - Controls Over Classified Documents for a Special Access Program at Lockheed Corporation
claims.sourceText: GAO accession 130581, statement of Martin M. Ferber, 24 July 1986
claims.text: The testimony closes: 'In summary, it appears inconsistent to us to establish a special access program because of security considerations and then afford it less document protection than normal classified programs.'
